title: Snowdrop and Bram's Goodnight Garden
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a green meadow, lived Snowdrop, a little white bunny, and Bram, a soft brown bear cub. Snowdrop was fluffy. She liked to whisper. Bram was warm. He loved hugs and long naps.

Every day they played in the sunshine. Snowdrop hopped. Bram lumbered. They played hide-and-seek, and their laughter was like little bells. They shared sweet berries by the stream. The meadow smelled of grass and warm fur.

Now the sun began to go down. It painted the sky with quiet colours. Snowdrop's eyes felt heavy. Bram yawned a big yawn. It was time for beds, and for the kind of hush that comes before dreams.

Until one day, as the last sleepy rays warmed their fur, Snowdrop had a gentle idea.

"Bram," she whispered, soft as a falling leaf, "let us say goodnight to the garden. Let us tell the sleepy flowers and the busy little bugs goodnight."

Bram made a rumble, low and pleased. "A trail of goodnights. Oh, Snowdrop. That sounds lovely."

Because of that, they walked to the garden's edge. The little daisies, bright all day, were nodding. Their petals curled closed. Snowdrop leaned close.

"Goodnight, sleepy daisy. Rest well."

Bram whispered to a ladybug snuggled on a leaf. "Goodnight, little ladybug. Dream of sunshine."

They said goodnight to the shy violets under the leaves. "Goodnight, shy violets."

They whispered to the tall grass, still swaying a little. "Goodnight, tall grass. Settle down now."

Moonlight drifted down in bits, like pale dust. The moonflowers were opening their pale faces. Snowdrop touched one petal.

"A goodnight kiss for the moonflower."

Bram found a patch of moss, tucked under a leaf, wonderfully soft. "Hush now, little moss. Settle down."

The garden listened. It did not clap. It only grew quieter, the way a room grows quieter when a blanket is pulled up.

Because of that, Snowdrop and Bram felt their own heads grow light. Each tiny goodnight made the path home feel slower and kinder. The garden seemed to sigh, a thank-you without words.

Until finally the big round moon peeked through the old oak and laid soft shadows on the path. Snowdrop snuggled into her nest of moss and leaves, nose twitching once, then still. Bram curled in his den, a warm hollow lined with earth, already slipping. They closed their eyes. The goodnights went with them, small and echoey, like bells heard from far away.

Ever since then, when the sun paints the sky that quiet colour, Snowdrop and Bram walk the same small trail. Daisy. Ladybug. Violet. Grass. Moonflower. Moss. Then their own beds. The dark comes, as dark does. The garden holds the whispers. Two little sleepers, safe as boats on a calm sea, drift, and the oak keeps watch, and nobody needs to say how powerful a goodnight is. The moss already knows.
